description: Baseline eval fixture for PP-004: how long it takes this second reference app to prove itself from a torn-down, clean-environment starting state, and what evidence backs each R0-R3 control. Comparable to evidence/../../nextjs-postgres-crud/evidence/pp-003-eval-fixture.json — same task-board domain, same profile, a materially different stack (React/Vite SPA + FastAPI + SQLAlchemy/Alembic instead of Next.js + Prisma).

stack.capabilityPack: none — no capability pack exists yet for this stack; auth/RBAC is built directly into backend/app (see docs/runbook.md)

cleanEnvironmentRehearsal.scope: docker compose down -v, fresh Postgres, alembic upgrade head, seed, docker build --no-cache, run, health check, smoke test, teardown

migrationRollbackRehearsal.scope: verify schema, alembic downgrade base, verify dropped, alembic upgrade head + seed, verify restored

readinessCheck.result: PASS (25/25 controls) — every R0-R3 control has real, checked evidence, reached on the first push (no fix-iterate rounds needed against real CI, unlike PP-003's three). One genuine finding along the way, caught and fixed before pushing: pip-audit's initial run against the pinned lockfile found 7 known advisories (PYSEC-2026-161/248/249/1941/1942/2280/2281) in a transitively-pinned starlette version pulled in by fastapi's loose >=0.46.0 bound; fixed by pinning starlette directly to >=1.6,<1.7 (see docs/security-notes.md), not documented-and-ignored. Also surfaced and fixed a real command-line-tooling gap unrelated to the app itself: development/state.json's PP-003 verification command was missing --root and would not actually reproduce a pass as originally written (file evidence resolves relative to --root, which defaults to cwd) — corrected in PP-003's own state.json entry, without changing its already-recorded pass outcome.
